query_normalized: evaluating the statistical validity of crowdsourced labels statistics
rationale: This paper satisfies criterion (a) and (b) because it empirically analyzes the statistical properties of "human-annotated labels" (the crowdsourced population) and specifically investigates "second-order statistics" (covariance terms) to characterize the validity and noise structure of these labels, which directly addresses the user's query about evaluating the statistical validity of such data.
